name: helipod-mcp

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: Projects this API key can reach, each with its environments (production, staging, ...). Start here to find an environmentId.

tools.name: get_project
tools.description: One project with its environments (ids and names). Use it to find an environmentId when you already know the project.

projectId.description: Project id (UUID)

tools.name: create_project
tools.description: Create a project (free) with its default production environment. Needs a whole-account key (a key limited to one project gets 403). Pass an idempotencyKey when retrying.

idempotencyKey.description: Idempotency-Key: a retry with the same value returns the first result instead of doing it twice

tools.name: update_project
tools.description: Change a project's name and/or description.

projectId.description: Project id (UUID)

tools.name: delete_project
tools.description: Delete an EMPTY project and its environments and shared variables. Irreversible. Refused (409 PROJECT_NOT_EMPTY) while it still has services, databases, VPS or other resources: those must be deleted first. Needs a whole-account key. Only after the user confirms; confirm must be the project's exact name.

projectId.description: Project id (UUID)

tools.name: create_environment
tools.description: Add an environment (e.g. staging) to a project. Free; services in it are billed as usual once deployed.

projectId.description: Project id (UUID)

tools.name: rename_environment
tools.description: Rename an environment (names are unique within the project).

tools.name: delete_environment
tools.description: Delete an EMPTY environment (409 ENVIRONMENT_NOT_EMPTY while it has services: delete them first). Irreversible. Only after the user confirms; confirm must be the environment's exact name.

tools.name: list_project_variables
tools.description: Variables shared by every service of a project (referenced as ${{shared.KEY}}). Secret values are never returned (value is null).

projectId.description: Project id (UUID)

tools.name: set_project_variables
tools.description: Create or update shared project variables (other keys are kept). Mark credentials as secrets (once secret, always secret). Services pick them up on their next deploy.

projectId.description: Project id (UUID)

tools.name: delete_project_variable
tools.description: Remove one shared project variable. Services that reference it lose it on their next deploy: check with the user.

projectId.description: Project id (UUID)

tools.name: list_services
tools.description: Services (containers) in an environment: status, source, resources, domains, latest deployment and daily cost.

tools.name: get_service
tools.description: One service with its source, settings, resources, domains, latest deployment and daily cost.

tools.name: create_service
tools.description: Create a service from a container image, a public Git repository or an inline Dockerfile, and (unless deploy=false) start its first deploy. COSTS MONEY once deployed (billed daily from the wallet): call with dryRun=true first, show the dailyCost to the user and get their OK.

name.description: Service name (letters, digits, _ -; starts with a letter). Also used in references like ${{name.KEY}}

image.description: Container image, e.g. nginx:alpine or ghcr.io/acme/app:1.2

repo.description: Public HTTPS Git repository URL (instead of image)

rootDirectory.description: Monorepo: folder to build, e.g. apps/web

ports.description: Ports to expose; each public http port gets an HTTPS *.helipod.app domain

public.description: http ports: give it a *.helipod.app domain (default true)

healthcheckPath.description: HTTP path answering 2xx when ready, e.g. /health

deploy.description: false: create without deploying (nothing is charged)

dryRun.description: true: return the daily cost (IDR) only, change nothing

idempotencyKey.description: Idempotency-Key: a retry with the same value returns the first result instead of doing it twice

tools.name: update_service
tools.description: Rename a service or change its start command, root directory, health check or startup dependencies. Settings apply on the next deploy (needsRedeploy). Renaming breaks references like ${{oldName.KEY}} in other services' variables: the response lists them in warnings.

name.description: New service name (letters, digits, _ -; starts with a letter; unique in the environment)

dependsOn.description: Service ids (same environment) to wait for at startup

tools.name: delete_service
tools.description: Stop and delete a service with its domains and volumes. Volume data is lost.

tools.name: deploy_service
tools.description: Start a new deployment (Git services build the latest commit). COSTS MONEY: charges today's cost when the build starts, refunded if it fails. dryRun=true returns the cost only. The deployment runs in the background; get_deployment returns its status.

dryRun.description: true: return the daily cost (IDR) only, change nothing

idempotencyKey.description: Idempotency-Key: a retry with the same value returns the first result instead of doing it twice

tools.name: list_deployments
tools.description: Recent deployments of a service, newest first.

tools.name: get_deployment
tools.description: Status of one deployment: pending, running, success, failed, cancelled or removed. Poll every few seconds until it settles.

tools.name: get_deployment_logs
tools.description: The build and rollout log of a deployment. Read it when a deployment failed.

tools.name: restart_service
tools.description: Restart a running service's containers without building again.

tools.name: list_variables
tools.description: Environment variables of a service. Secret values are never returned (value is null).

tools.name: set_variables
tools.description: Create or update variables (other keys are kept). Mark credentials as secrets. Applies on the next deploy.

tools.name: delete_variable
tools.description: Remove one variable. Applies on the next deploy.

tools.name: list_service_domains
tools.description: Public domains and TCP ports of a service, with DNS instructions for custom domains.

tools.name: add_service_domain
tools.description: Add a free *.helipod.app domain (kind=helipod) or your own domain (kind=custom) to a port. For custom domains, the response's dns field is the DNS record the domain needs.

tools.name: remove_service_domain
tools.description: Remove a domain from a service.

tools.name: get_scale
tools.description: Replicas, CPU, RAM, autoscaling and daily cost of a service.

tools.name: scale_service
tools.description: Change replicas, CPU or RAM (applies right away). COSTS MONEY on increase: call with dryRun=true first to show currentDailyCost vs newDailyCost and get the user's OK.

dryRun.description: true: return the daily cost (IDR) only, change nothing

tools.name: list_volumes
tools.description: Persistent volumes of a service.

tools.name: add_volume
tools.description: Add persistent storage mounted at a path (billed daily per GB, first 1 GB free). Applies on the next deploy.

tools.name: delete_volume
tools.description: Remove a volume; its data is lost on the next deploy.

tools.name: resize_volume
tools.description: Change a volume's size (1-50 GB; never below the space already used). A larger volume COSTS MONEY: it raises the daily cost, charged pro rata when the service is redeployed and in full from the next renewal. dryRun=true returns currentDailyCost and newDailyCost (IDR) without changing anything. Applies on the next deploy.

sizeGb.description: New size in GB (give sizeGb or sizeMb)

sizeMb.description: New size in MB, a multiple of 1024

dryRun.description: true: return the daily cost (IDR) only, change nothing

tools.name: update_service_domain_port
tools.description: Point an existing domain of a service (from list_service_domains) at another container port. Applies on the next deploy when needsRedeploy is true.

tools.name: get_function_code
tools.description: Source code of a function service (409 NOT_A_FUNCTION for other services).

tools.name: set_function_code
tools.description: Replace the whole source code of a function service (up to 512 KB). The previous code is overwritten (get_function_code returns the current code). Runs after the next deploy (deploy_service).

tools.name: list_secret_files
tools.description: Secret files mounted into a service (name, file name, mount path). Contents are write-only and never returned.

tools.name: add_secret_file
tools.description: Upload a file (certificate, key, credentials JSON, config) that is mounted read-only into the service at mountPath. Content is base64 of the file's bytes, at most 10 MB; it is stored as a secret and can never be read back. Applies on the next deploy.

mountPath.description: Absolute path in the container, e.g. /etc/secrets/service-account.json

contentBase64.description: The file's bytes in standard base64

tools.name: update_secret_file
tools.description: Replace a secret file's contents (base64) and/or change its mount path or label. The old contents are overwritten. Applies on the next deploy.

tools.name: delete_secret_file
tools.description: Delete a secret file; it is gone from the service after the next deploy and cannot be recovered (contents are never readable).

tools.name: get_service_logs
tools.description: What the running service printed, newest first. Use filter to search (e.g. 'error').

tools.name: get_service_metrics
tools.description: CPU, memory and network over time plus current values and restarts.

tools.name: list_templates
tools.description: One-click templates (WordPress, n8n, Postgres, Umami, ...). Use the slug with deploy_template.

tools.name: deploy_template
tools.description: Create every service of a template in an environment and deploy them. COSTS MONEY (each service is billed daily).

idempotencyKey.description: Idempotency-Key: a retry with the same value returns the first result instead of doing it twice

tools.name: create_stack
tools.description: Create several connected services from a template spec ({ version: 1, inputs?, services: [...] }) and deploy them in dependency order. COSTS MONEY: dryRun=true first. See https://docs.helipod.io/docs/container-api/templates-and-stacks

dryRun.description: true: return the daily cost (IDR) only, change nothing

idempotencyKey.description: Idempotency-Key: a retry with the same value returns the first result instead of doing it twice

tools.name: list_database_plans
tools.description: Managed Postgres plans: price (IDR), included compute hours and storage, maximum CU. Free is the default; paid plans are prepaid credits that never expire.

tools.name: list_databases
tools.description: Managed Postgres databases in the projects this key can reach: status, plan and remaining credits, region, branches per environment.

tools.name: get_database
tools.description: One database with its plan, compute settings and branches.

tools.name: create_database
tools.description: Create the managed Postgres database of a project (free plan; one database per project, one branch per environment). Returns the existing one if the project already has it.

tools.name: delete_database
tools.description: Delete a database with ALL its data and branches. Irreversible. Only after the user confirms; confirm must be the database name.

tools.name: get_database_connection
tools.description: Connection string (postgresql://…, pooled, SSL) and its parts for an environment's branch. Contains the password: store it as a secret variable (e.g. DATABASE_URL via set_variables secrets), never print it unless asked.

environmentId.description: Environment id (from list_projects). Omit for the primary (production) branch.

tools.name: list_database_branches
tools.description: Branches of a database, one per environment (production is the primary).

tools.name: create_database_branch
tools.description: Give an environment (e.g. staging) its own branch: a copy of the source environment's data at this moment (the primary when omitted).

tools.name: delete_database_branch
tools.description: Delete an environment's branch and its data. The primary (production) branch cannot be deleted.

tools.name: get_database_settings
tools.description: Compute settings (paid plans): minCu (floor), maxCu (autoscaling ceiling), suspendTimeoutSeconds (idle time before scaling to zero), the plan's maximum CU.

tools.name: update_database_settings
tools.description: Change compute for every branch (paid plans). A minCu above zero keeps compute running and uses credits while idle: run with dryRun first and show idleComputeHoursPerMonth.

dryRun.description: true = only check and show the result or price; nothing changes

tools.name: upgrade_database
tools.description: Buy a paid plan or top up credits. COSTS MONEY from the wallet: call with dryRun first, show price and wallet balance after, and get the user's explicit OK.

plan.description: Plan code (e.g. STARTER) or id from list_database_plans

dryRun.description: true = only check and show the result or price; nothing changes

tools.name: suspend_database
tools.description: Stop the database's compute (connections fail until resumed).

tools.name: resume_database
tools.description: Start a suspended database again.

tools.name: get_database_usage
tools.description: This period's compute (CU-hours), storage, history and network, plus the plan's remaining credits.

tools.name: get_database_stats
tools.description: Live compute stats of an environment's branch over the last hours: CPU, memory, rows read/written, cache hit rate, connections. grouping min/hour/day sets the point size.

environmentId.description: Environment id (from list_projects). Omit for the primary (production) branch.

tools.name: get_database_balance
tools.description: Credit left on the paid plan: compute (CU-hours) and storage remaining. Zero on the free plan. Top up with upgrade_database.

tools.name: list_database_tables
tools.description: Tables and views in the public schema of an environment's branch.

environmentId.description: Environment id (from list_projects). Omit for the primary (production) branch.

tools.name: describe_database_table
tools.description: Columns of a table (name, type, nullable, default).

environmentId.description: Environment id (from list_projects). Omit for the primary (production) branch.

tools.name: browse_database_table
tools.description: Rows of a table, a page at a time (limit up to 200, offset to page). Read-only. Rows are returned as stored, including any sensitive columns.

environmentId.description: Environment id (from list_projects). Omit for the primary (production) branch.

tools.name: query_database
tools.description: Run a read-only SQL statement (SELECT, EXPLAIN, SHOW…) in a read-only transaction; up to 200 rows. Use $1, $2… placeholders with params. Statements that change data are refused (execute_database_sql runs those).

environmentId.description: Environment id (from list_projects). Omit for the primary (production) branch.

tools.name: classify_database_sql
tools.description: What a SQL statement is (command, e.g. select / update / drop) and whether it writes, WITHOUT running it. It reports what a statement would change before execute_database_sql runs it; readOnly statements can run with query_database.

tools.name: execute_database_sql
tools.description: Run a statement that changes data or schema (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, CREATE, ALTER, DROP…). classify_database_sql reports what a statement does without running it. It runs on the chosen environment's branch.

environmentId.description: Environment id (from list_projects). Omit for the primary (production) branch.

tools.name: list_vps_plans
tools.description: VPS plans with CPU, RAM, disk, OS templates and the price this account pays (effectiveMonthly, IDR).

tools.name: list_vps
tools.description: Servers this key can reach, with status and public IP.

tools.name: get_vps
tools.description: One server: status, IP, size, plan, expiry, last job. Poll it after an action until status is running, stopped, terminated or error.

tools.name: create_vps
tools.description: Order a server. COSTS MONEY right away (the whole billing period is charged from the wallet; refunded if provisioning fails). Show the plan price from list_vps_plans and get the user's explicit OK first. Provisioning takes a few minutes: poll get_vps.

osType.description: From the plan's osTemplates, e.g. ubuntu

rootPassword.description: 12-30 characters with upper and lower case letters, a digit and one of ! @ # $ % ^ *

tools.name: vps_power
tools.description: Power action on a server. stop and restart interrupt whatever runs on it.

tools.name: reinstall_vps
tools.description: Wipe the disk and install an operating system. ALL DATA ON THE SERVER IS LOST.

rootPassword.description: 12-30 characters with upper and lower case letters, a digit and one of ! @ # $ % ^ *

tools.name: reset_vps_password
tools.description: Set a new root (or Administrator) password. Stored only when the reset succeeds.

rootPassword.description: 12-30 characters with upper and lower case letters, a digit and one of ! @ # $ % ^ *

tools.name: get_vps_credentials
tools.description: Login details: host, user (root, or Administrator on Windows), port, protocol (ssh or rdp) and password. The response contains the root password.

tools.name: terminate_vps
tools.description: Delete a server permanently. ALL DATA IS LOST and there is no refund for the remaining period.

tools.name: get_vps_renewal_options
tools.description: Prices to renew a server for each billing period.

tools.name: renew_vps
tools.description: Extend a server's paid period. COSTS MONEY: show the price from get_vps_renewal_options and get the user's OK.

tools.name: upgrade_vps
tools.description: Move a server to a larger plan in the same family and region. COSTS MONEY (the difference for the days left) and restarts the server. planId must be one listed by get_vps_upgrade_options, which also gives the price in IDR; the server restarts during the upgrade.

tools.name: get_vps_upgrade_options
tools.description: Plans this server can move to (same family and region) with the price to pay now for the days left (IDR). upgrade_vps accepts only a planId from this list.

tools.name: rename_vps
tools.description: Change a server's display name (3-50 characters). Nothing on the server changes.

tools.name: get_vps_metrics
tools.description: CPU, memory, disk and network use of a server. range (1h default, 6h, 24h, 7d, 30d) applies to servers with history; others return their latest reading.

tools.name: toggle_vps_auto_renew
tools.description: Flip auto-renew on or off; the response gives the new value.

tools.name: list_firewall_rules
tools.description: Inbound firewall rules of a server.

tools.name: add_firewall_rules
tools.description: Add inbound rules. Port: a number, a range a-b, a comma list, or ALL.

tools.name: remove_firewall_rules
tools.description: Remove rules by id (from list_firewall_rules). All must match or nothing is removed.

tools.name: list_vps_ports
tools.description: Port forwards of a server (servers on a shared IP): the public port range it may use and each forward (protocol, public port, internal port, domain for http/https routes). Not available on every server type.

tools.name: add_vps_port
tools.description: Forward a public port to the server: protocol tcp/udp/both uses a port inside the server's portRange (from list_vps_ports); protocol http/https routes a domain on port 80/443 to internalPort (point the domain's DNS at the server's IP first). The server must be running.

port.description: Public port (tcp/udp: inside portRange; http=80, https=443)

internalPort.description: Port on the server (default: same as port)

domain.description: http/https only: the domain to route, e.g. app.example.com

tools.name: remove_vps_port
tools.description: Remove a port forward (id from list_vps_ports). Whatever reaches the server through it stops working.

tools.name: list_vps_ssh_keys
tools.description: SSH public keys allowed to log in as root, by fingerprint (SHA256:…), with type and comment. Not available on every server type.

tools.name: add_vps_ssh_key
tools.description: Allow an SSH PUBLIC key (e.g. the contents of ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub) to log in as root; at most 10 per server. Never send a private key: it is refused. The server must be running.

tools.name: remove_vps_ssh_key
tools.description: Remove an SSH key by fingerprint (from list_vps_ssh_keys). Whoever logs in with it loses access (another key or the root password still works).

tools.name: set_vps_ssh
tools.description: Turn SSH access to the server on or off (no change when it is already in that state). Turning it off locks out every SSH session and key. The server must be running.

tools.name: list_snapshots
tools.description: Disk snapshots of a server.

tools.name: create_snapshot
tools.description: Take a snapshot of the server's disk (free; the plan limits how many you keep).

tools.name: apply_snapshot
tools.description: Roll the server's disk back to a snapshot. Everything written since is lost.

tools.name: delete_snapshot
tools.description: Delete a snapshot permanently (it can no longer be rolled back to).

tools.name: list_backup_plans
tools.description: Daily VPS backup plans: storage quota, priceMonthly and priceYearly (IDR), how many daily/weekly/monthly restore points are kept. Use it for the price before activate_vps_backup.

tools.name: get_vps_backup
tools.description: Backup of one server: plan, period and price, auto-renew, storage used vs quota, last backup, next run, manual runs left today, the job running now. null when backups are off; eligible/reason say whether this server can have them (Linux only).

tools.name: activate_vps_backup
tools.description: Turn on daily backups for a running Linux server. COSTS MONEY right away: the whole period (1 or 12 months) is charged from the wallet and there is no dry run. Prices (priceMonthly / priceYearly, IDR) are in list_backup_plans. The server must be running.

scheduleHour.description: Hour of the daily backup, 0-23 WIB (UTC+7)

alignWithVps.description: Monthly only: make the first period end with the server's own expiry (prorated price)

tools.name: update_vps_backup
tools.description: Change the backup plan, the daily hour or auto-renew. A larger plan COSTS MONEY now (the difference for the days left, charged from the wallet): show the new plan's price from list_backup_plans and get the user's OK. A smaller plan starts at the next renewal.

tools.name: cancel_vps_backup
tools.description: Stop renewing the server's backups. Backups keep running until the paid period ends; after that and a grace period the backups are DELETED and can no longer be restored. (update_vps_backup autoRenew=true undoes it before the end.)

tools.name: run_vps_backup
tools.description: Start a backup now, in addition to the daily one (limited per day: see manualRunsLeft in get_vps_backup). Runs in the background: follow it with list_vps_backup_runs.

tools.name: list_vps_backup_runs
tools.description: Recent backup, restore and download jobs of a server with status, timing and errors.

tools.name: list_vps_restore_points
tools.description: Restore points (backups kept) of a server: id, time taken, kind (daily/weekly/monthly/manual), size added, file count.

tools.name: browse_vps_backup_files
tools.description: List the files and folders at a path inside a restore point (names, types, sizes, dates; not file contents). Use it to pick paths for restore_vps_backup or prepare_vps_backup_download.

tools.name: restore_vps_backup
tools.description: Restore from a restore point. mode=full puts the WHOLE disk back to that moment: everything written since is LOST and the server is offline while it restores. mode=files restores 1-50 paths: target=folder (default) puts them in a separate folder on the server, target=inplace OVERWRITES the current files. Files at those paths are overwritten. Runs in the background: follow it with list_vps_backup_runs.

paths.description: mode=files: files or folders to restore

items.description: Absolute path inside the backup, e.g. /etc/nginx or /var/www/index.html

tools.name: prepare_vps_backup_download
tools.description: Pack up to 20 files or folders from a restore point into a download (a few per day). Returns a download id and status; poll get_vps_backup_download until status is ready, then give the user the link. Never fetch or print the file contents.

items.description: Absolute path inside the backup, e.g. /etc/nginx or /var/www/index.html

tools.name: get_vps_backup_download
tools.description: Status of a prepared backup download; when ready, a short-lived url for the user to open (it expires at expiresAt). The link is for the user to download in a browser.

tools.name: search_domain
tools.description: Is a domain name available to register? No key needed.

tools.name: domain_prices
tools.description: Registration, renewal and transfer prices per extension (IDR, VAT included) and the yearly WHOIS privacy price.

tools.name: list_my_domains
tools.description: Domains registered on this account, with status, expiry and nameservers. Needs a whole-account key with the Domain API.

tools.name: get_domain
tools.description: One registered domain.

tools.name: check_registrant
tools.description: Whether the account's domain owner details are complete (required before the first registration) and which fields are missing. Fill them with update_registrant.

tools.name: update_registrant
tools.description: Set the account's domain owner (registrant) details the registrar needs: name, phone, addressLine1, city, state, countryCode and postalCode are required for a complete profile (organization, addressLine2 and fax are optional). Send only fields to change. These are personal details of the domain owner, stored as given. The answer says whether the details are now complete and which fields are still missing (it never echoes them).

tools.name: register_domain
tools.description: Register a domain for 1 year. COSTS MONEY from the wallet. Check search_domain, and that the owner details are complete (check_registrant / update_registrant). dryRun=true returns the price and walletBalanceAfter without charging or changing anything. The dry run includes WHOIS privacy when whoisProtection is true.

dryRun.description: true = return the exact price (IDR, VAT included) and the wallet balance after it; nothing is charged or registered

tools.name: transfer_domain
tools.description: Transfer a domain from another registrar (adds 1 year). COSTS MONEY from the wallet. Needs the domain's auth code. dryRun=true returns the price and walletBalanceAfter without charging or changing anything.

dryRun.description: true = return the exact price (IDR, VAT included) and the wallet balance after it; nothing is charged or registered

tools.name: renew_domain
tools.description: Renew a domain for 1 year (plus WHOIS privacy when it is on). COSTS MONEY from the wallet. dryRun=true returns the price and walletBalanceAfter without charging or changing anything.

dryRun.description: true = return the exact price (IDR, VAT included) and the wallet balance after it; nothing is charged or registered

tools.name: list_dns_records
tools.description: DNS records of a registered domain.

tools.name: set_dns_records
tools.description: Replace ALL DNS records of the domain with this list. Records not included are deleted (list_dns_records returns the current ones).

name.description: "@" for the domain itself, or a label like "www"

tools.name: delete_dns_record
tools.description: Delete one DNS record (name, type and current content must match).

tools.name: set_nameservers
tools.description: Point the domain to other nameservers (2 to 5). Helipod DNS records stop applying while external nameservers are set.

tools.name: enable_whois_privacy
tools.description: Hide the owner's details in WHOIS. COSTS MONEY (the whois_protection price per year).

tools.name: get_domain_price
tools.description: Registration, renewal and transfer price (IDR, VAT included) and WHOIS privacy price of one extension, by the price id from domain_prices.

priceId.description: Price id (the id of a domain_prices row)

tools.name: whois_lookup
tools.description: Public WHOIS record of any domain name: registrar, dates, status, nameservers. Availability is checked by search_domain.

tools.name: update_dns_record
tools.description: Set one DNS record (by name and type) to new content, leaving the other records as they are. Changes one record and leaves the others as they are (list_dns_records returns record ids).

name.description: "@" for the domain itself, or a label like "www"

tools.name: list_child_nameservers
tools.description: Child nameservers (glue records like ns1.yourdomain.com) of a registered domain, with their IP addresses.

tools.name: create_child_nameserver
tools.description: Create a child nameserver (glue record) under the domain, e.g. hostname ns1 → ns1.yourdomain.com pointing to an IP. Only needed to run your own nameservers on this domain.

tools.name: update_child_nameserver
tools.description: Change a child nameserver's name or IP address. Domains using it as a nameserver follow the new IP.

tools.name: delete_child_nameserver
tools.description: Delete a child nameserver. Any domain still using it as a nameserver stops resolving: check with the user first.

tools.name: get_whois_privacy
tools.description: Whether WHOIS privacy (hiding the owner's details) is on for a domain.

tools.name: disable_whois_privacy
tools.description: Turn WHOIS privacy off: the owner's name, address, email and phone become PUBLIC in WHOIS (no refund; turning it back on with enable_whois_privacy costs money).

tools.name: email_status
tools.description: Email service of the key's project: plan, usage today and this month, limits, counts. activated false = email is not set up yet: start it with buy_email_plan.

projectId.description: Project whose email to use. Only needed with a whole-account key that reaches several projects with email.

tools.name: list_email_plans
tools.description: Email plans: code, monthly price (IDR), sending quota, mailboxes and inbox storage, billing cycles (1/3/6/12 months). Use the code with buy_email_plan or change_email_plan.

tools.name: get_email_plan
tools.description: The project's current email plan and subscription: plan, period, expiry, auto-renew, extra mailboxes and storage. plan is null when there is none.

projectId.description: Project whose email to use. Only needed with a whole-account key that reaches several projects with email.

tools.name: buy_email_plan

instructions:
Helipod is a cloud platform (Indonesia): containers, managed Postgres databases, VPS, domains, email and an AI gateway, billed from a prepaid wallet in Rupiah.
- Start with list_projects to find projects and environment ids. Account tools (get_wallet, invoices, statements, notifications, get_project_activity, support tickets) cover the account; AI tools (list_ai_models, get_ai_overview, get_ai_usage, AI keys, top-ups) cover the AI gateway.
- Anything that costs money (create/deploy/scale services, resize volumes, upgrade a database plan, create/renew/upgrade VPS, VPS backups, register/renew/transfer domains, email plans and inbox add-ons, AI top-ups and auto top-up): call it with dryRun=true first (or the price lookup when it has no dry run), tell the user the cost in IDR and the wallet balance after, and wait for an explicit yes before the real call. Never treat silence or an earlier general OK as a yes.
- Destructive tools (delete, terminate, reinstall, rollback, restore a backup, replace DNS, revoke a key, remove an SSH key or port forward, send a broadcast, execute_database_sql): confirm with the user and name what will be lost. Before execute_database_sql, run classify_database_sql.
- Email: when a project has no email yet (email_status shows activated false) or its plan ended, start it with buy_email_plan (dryRun first; the FREE plan costs nothing, still confirm). That also sets email up for the project; then add and verify a sending domain.
- Before replacing all DNS records (set_dns_records), read list_dns_records and keep every record the user still needs. Before sending or scheduling a broadcast, tell the user how many contacts it reaches. Before deleting or replacing code, files or variables, read the current value. After renaming a service, fix the variable references listed in warnings.
- Databases: get_database_connection returns a password; put it in a secret variable (DATABASE_URL) instead of code or chat.
- Deploys and VPS actions run in the background: poll get_deployment / get_vps until they settle; on a failed deploy read get_deployment_logs.
- Never print secrets (passwords, secret variable values, secret files) unless the user asks for them. Domain owner details are personal data: use only what the user gave.
- Errors come back as { status, code, error }: 401/403 means the key lacks access (keys choose products and projects in Settings → API keys; wallet, invoices, tickets and AI money need a whole-account key: with a sign-in, reconnect and choose Whole account), 402 means plan limit or low balance.
Docs: https://docs.helipod.io
stderr: helipod-mcp: set HELIPOD_API_KEY (enable the Email API on it for the email tools). Create keys in the Helipod dashboard: Project → Settings → API keys.
